oneParagraph: P-178's data half is DONE and verified on production: the declared-roll marking is a real loader step, the 8-26 certified export loaded exactly as pre-registered (134591 upserted / 375 inserted / 390 marked, identifiers intact, dollar movement matching the decision doc to the dollar), and the marker's serve-side logic is PROVEN CORRECT. P-178's serving half (step 6, re-bake + publish Hays tier-1) is BLOCKED, not by P-178 but by a P-180/walk conflict the pin bump exposed: P-180 excludes 'hollow account-keyed nodes' from the bake, so those nodes keep a stale publishRunId, and the verify-walk requires the current run id on every parcel it sweeps -- including an earned retirement. Production was never written to. The blocker is handed to the P-180 lane.

blockerMechanism: P-180 (hauska-factory #145 + LDT #683/#684, inside the new pin range) drops hollow account-keyed nodes from the bake's work list on a gate-blocked county (nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts ~379-403, isAccountKeyedNodeId).
An excluded node is never rewritten, so it keeps the PREVIOUS run's publishRunId -- measured: 48209 tier1 is split 116421 rows at the current run vs 56629 at the previous one.

The verify-walk reads the SERVED body and requires the CURRENT run id (responseCarriesPublishRunId), and it requires it on RETIRED rows too -- the RECORD_RETIRED branch checks the stamp before returning pass (verify-walk.mjs 508-511).

The street sweep ('same-situs-street:multi-anchor', anchors = gold + the county's smoke parcels) samples whatever shares a street with the anchors; hollow nodes live on those same streets, so the sweep inevitably includes some, and they fail.

84629 confirmed: not in txgio_parcel, carries an EARNED retirement {status:retired, verdict:absent-verified, lastSeenTaxYear:2025, asOf:2026-09-14T03:31:56Z} written by the FIRST run under the OLD pin (which still baked every node). Under the new pin it is not baked at all, so that retirement can never carry a fresh stamp.
run3_fwv5s_theRealBlocker.notTheMarkedAccounts: 84629-84639 are NOT in the marked-390. They are the broader 'left the declared roll, last seen 2025' population. The marker itself is unaffected.
run3_fwv5s_theRealBlocker.conclusion: Hays' publish walk CANNOT pass under the new pin: any sweep touching an excluded node fails on a stamp that by construction will never be refreshed. This was invisible before because the old pin baked all 173050 nodes with one stamp.

falsifierCorrected.original: CP4's 'marked accounts served with a real cadRoll dollar' count (305) 'must go to 0'.
falsifierCorrected.verdict: MIS-SPECIFIED -- a bare-number category error, and it is corrected here rather than quietly dropped. It equated cad_property.prop_id with the node id in place_key. For a gate-blocked county those are two DIFFERENT published numbering systems that only coincidentally share digits -- the exact collision SEED_BLOCKED_FIPS/P-177 exists to refuse. The count could never reach 0, and its staying at 305 never indicated a servable marked dollar.
falsifierCorrected.supersededBy: The crosswalk-resolved check in p178MarkerProvenWorking: resolve the node's OWN geo_id to the account that actually owns that property_number, and verify the marked account contributes nothing. That is the check that actually tests the marker.
falsifierCorrected.statedBecause: The pre-registered falsifier was wrong, and a close that reported '305 -> 305, FAIL' without this correction would misrepresent a working fix as a broken one.

leave_behind.finding: P-180's hollow-account-keyed-node exclusion and the verify-walk's current-run-stamp requirement are mutually unsatisfiable for Hays on the post-#683 pin. The walk cannot pass while any swept node is one P-180 excludes.
leave_behind.why: Excluded nodes are never rewritten, so their publishRunId is permanently stale, and the walk requires the current id even on an earned retirement.
leave_behind.nextStep: P-180 lane's call. Two viable shapes, neither taken here (operator ruled 'report and stop'): (B) keep excluding hollow nodes from the fact build but still retire them with the CURRENT run id in a cheap pass, so the stamp the walk wants exists; or (A) teach the walk not to require a fresh stamp on a node the bake no longer owns, or to accept an earned retirement whose stamp predates the run. (B) preserves both invariants. Labelled a real conflict, not a one-off flake: it will recur on every Hays republish.

scopeBasis: The dispatch named three deliverables (marking as a loader step, the vintage label map, the deploy) plus a dry-run and a duplicate-account report; all were completed and the production apply was executed on the operator's explicit 'go' and verified against pre-registered falsifiers. Step 6 (re-bake/publish + seven reads) was the dispatch's own next step, and it was pursued as far as the evidence allowed: the pin-bump remedy was operator-approved mid-mission, and a second and third staging publish were run to isolate the failures. The mission stopped where it did on the operator's explicit 'report and stop' ruling, rather than continuing into the P-180 lane's code -- P-180 is a different lane's surface, the conflict is a design question about which invariant wins, and the previous P-177 close already records the pattern of this lane not writing into work it does not own.
